Assess MCMC convergence for a TreePPL analysis

Source: R/post-process.R
tp_mcmc_convergence.Rd

Computes per-parameter effective sample size (ESS) and, when multiple runs are available, the upper limit of the Gelman-Rubin potential scale reduction factor (R-hat), using the coda package.

Usage

tp_mcmc_convergence(treeppl_out)

Arguments

treeppl_out

A tibble produced by tp_parse_mcmc(), in either long or wide format.

Value

A tibble with one row per parameter, containing:

parameter

Parameter name.

ess

Effective sample size, pooled across all runs.

rhat_upper

Upper limit of the Gelman-Rubin R-hat statistic. Only computed when treeppl_out contains more than one run; otherwise NA, with a message explaining why.

Details

Output produced from an unnamed return type in TreePPL (.tppl file) is not supported and will raise an error, since there is no reliable way to distinguish multiple parameters.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{

# CRBD model using MCMC
run_mcmc <- tp_run(
sampler = tp_compile(model = "crbd", method = "mcmc"),
data = tp_data(data_input = "crbd"),
iterations = 10,
n_runs = 2,
n_processes = 2
)

# tp_run() already returns the output of tp_parse_mcmc(), so we can call
# tp_mcmc_convergence() directly:
tp_mcmc_convergence(run_mcmc)
} # }
